case_title: AK Devaiah v. State of Karnataka
accused_caste: Kodava community (as stated by the accused)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.498-A, s.304-B; Dowry Prohibition Act s.3, s.4, s.6
weapon: None mentioned (deceased set herself on fire with kerosene)
evidence_type: Oral testimony of PWs 1-3 (sister, brother, sister's husband); medical (post-mortem); recovery of ornaments; inquest statements
aggravating_circumstances: Death within about eleven months of marriage; dowry demand and cruelty alleged and accepted; victim set herself on fire
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of all charges (IPC ss.498-A and 304-B; Dowry Prohibition Act ss.3, 4, 6)
high_court_outcome: State's appeal allowed, acquittal set aside; convicted under IPC ss.498-A, 304-B and DP Act ss.3, 4, 6; 7 years for s.304-B; 5 years and Rs 15,000 fine for s.3 DP Act
offence_finally_established: Dowry death (IPC s.304-B); cruelty (IPC s.498-A); Dowry Prohibition Act ss.3, 4 and 6
neutral_facts: The victim, a woman, was married to the accused in April 1989 and lived in the accused's house, where she also worked for a private company. About three months before her death, the accused and the victim reportedly quarrelled because she had not become pregnant after marriage. The prosecution alleged that before the marriage the accused demanded cash of Rs 15,000 and gold and silver ornaments. Part of the cash was handed over before the wedding and more at the wedding, and all ornaments except one pair of gold bangles were given. The balance was promised after marriage. The prosecution alleged that the accused drank liquor and subjected the victim to mental and physical cruelty over the demand for the balance dowry. In March 1990, about eleven months after the marriage, the victim set herself on fire with kerosene in the house early in the morning. The accused informed the police of the unnatural death. An inquest was held by an executive magistrate, who recorded statements from the victim's blood relatives, and a case was registered. The post-mortem found 97% ante-mortem burns and death due to shock, with no signs of pregnancy. The accused was arrested, and during interrogation he led police to a pawnbroker's shop where the victim's pledged ornaments were recovered. Eleven prosecution witnesses were examined, including the victim's sister, brother and brother-in-law, who deposed about the dowry demand and cruelty.
offence_severity: Minimum 7 years; maximum imprisonment for life (IPC s.304-B)
physical_harm: Death; 97% ante-mortem burns with second and third degree burns over most of the body
financial_property_loss: Alleged dowry of Rs 15,000 cash and gold/silver ornaments; High Court ordered return of Rs 15,000 and the gold ornaments
motive: Demand for balance dowry and cruelty over it (accepted by the court on the evidence of PWs 1-3)
key_evidence_accepted: Consistent testimony of PWs 1-3 on dowry demand and cruelty; post-mortem findings; statutory presumption under s.304-B IPC
witness_credibility: PWs 1-3 found to have consistently deposed; court held the High Court's findings correct and the trial court's acquittal wholly perverse. The defence's interested-witness argument was not specifically addressed
post_offence_conduct: Reported the death to police within hours; ornaments were pledged and later recovered at his instance (as narrated, not separately analysed by the court)
trial_duration: offence: 16-3-1990; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 25.08.2005; Supreme Court: 14.10.2014
legal_representation: Appellant: Rajesh Mahale and Krutin R. Joshi; State of Karnataka: V.N. Raghupathy and Sanjay R. Hegde
investigation_status: Inquest held; suo motu FIR registered; investigation by PW10; charge sheet filed; trial completed; appeals decided by High Court and Supreme Court
procedural_irregularity: None noted by the court; the defence argued that independent witnesses were neither examined nor cited
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted; High Court: State's appeal allowed and accused convicted; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed, convictions upheld
prosecution_argument: PWs 1-3, as close relatives, are competent and natural witnesses with no reason to disbelieve them; dowry was demanded before marriage and the accused coerced the balance demand after marriage; the accused pledged the ornaments
defence_argument: Cash and jewellery were gifts for marriage expenses, not dowry; no dowry custom in the community; PWs 1-3 are interested and inconsistent with their inquest statements; no cruelty soon before death; recovery evidence inadmissible
legal_principle_applied: Dowry death under IPC s.304-B: death by burns or otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of marriage, with cruelty or harassment soon before death linked to a dowry demand; the statutory presumption shifts the onus to the accused to rebut it
precedent_relied_upon: Bansi Lal v. State of Haryana (2011) 11 SCC 359; Thanu Ram v. State of M.P. (2010) 10 SCC 353; Rajesh Bhatnagar v. State of Uttarakhand (2012) 7 SCC 91
judicial_aggravating_factors: None expressly weighed for sentence; court noted the death occurred within eleven months of marriage amid dowry-related cruelty
other_sentence_order: None separately ordered by the Supreme Court; the High Court's direction to return the dowry amount and gold ornaments was not disturbed
